quickFacts.text: SPAIN 1–0 ARGENTINA (aet) — Ferran Torres in the 106th wins the World Cup
The awards: Mbappé the Boot (10), Rodri the Ball, Simón the Glove, Cubarsí young player
The Crystal Ball retires at 6 winners from 11, two exact scores — and it called the champions

hero.headline: SPAIN, CHAMPIONS OF THE WORLD.
hero.standfirst: Sixteen years after Iniesta in Johannesburg, it happened again in extra time. Ferran Torres pounced on Nico Williams' knock-down in the 106th minute and drove the ball home, and the wall that conceded a single goal in seven games finally had its reward. Argentina, down to ten after Enzo Fernández's red card, were carried to extra time almost single-handedly by Emi Martínez's record eleven saves — but the repeat since 1962 never came. Spain have their second star. This is the last edition of The Morning Kickoff. What a summer it was.
hero.photoCaption: Ferran Torres — the 106th-minute strike that won the World Cup, "with the power of all the Spanish people"

briefing.text: The awards: Rodri takes the Golden Ball, Unai Simón the Golden Glove, 19-year-old Pau Cubarsí — who started every game — Young Player. Mbappé's 10 goals win the Boot: Messi, a ghost by his own standards, finished on 8 and fought back tears at the medals.
The final in numbers: Spain 65% possession, 20 shots, 12 on target; Argentina 2 shots, none on target, and no corner in the first ninety. Martínez's 11 saves are a World Cup final record.
The Crystal Ball signs off: 11 calls, 6 winners, 2 exact scorelines — and it named the champions on the last morning. The full scorecard is on page 3. Thank you for reading, every single morning.

events.text: Red card: Enzo Fernández (ARG), second yellow for a late challenge on Cubarsí in stoppage time — Argentina played extra time with ten

facts.text: Emi Martínez made 11 saves — a World Cup final record — including a stoppage-time wonder-stop from Yamal's free-kick
Argentina managed no shot on target, no corner and eight box touches across the whole night; Spain's xG read 1.94 to 0.20
Nico Williams had a goal disallowed for Merino's foul before setting up the winner; Lisandro Martínez went off injured before half-time

yesterday.report: Spain did to Argentina what they did to everyone: took the ball and never gave it back. But for ninety minutes the story belonged to Emiliano Martínez, who repelled everything — twelve Spanish efforts found the target and only the last one counted. Messi, shadowed and starved, barely touched the ball; the champions' plan was survival, and it very nearly reached penalties intact.
yesterday.report2: Then it cracked twice. Enzo Fernández's second yellow, for a late lunge on Cubarsí in stoppage time, left ten men for extra time. And in the 106th minute Porro crossed to the back post, Williams headed down, and Ferran Torres drove it high into the net. Martínez could do nothing, at last. Spain — one goal conceded in seven games, unbeaten now in 39 — are world champions for the second time, and the age of this team is only beginning.

star.name: Unai Simón
star.line: One goal conceded in an entire World Cup. The record clean-sheet streak, the France shutout, and a final where the wall held one last time.

aside.name: Lionel Messi
aside.line: A ghost on the night, in tears at the medals. No second star at 39 — but a Cup, a run of 14 unbeaten, and twenty years of mornings like these. What a way to have watched him.

yesterday.whatItMeans: Spain add a second star, sixteen years after 2010 — Euro champions and world champions at once. Argentina's era ends one game short of history. And with that, World Cup 26 is complete.
